About the Scholarship

Warwick’s Interdisciplinary Chancellors Scholarships support doctoral projects that connect research areas and align with a university Research Spotlight or Research Centre.

Research Areas

  • Eligible subjects across the university

Funding and Duration

ComponentDetails
FundingFull Home/International fees; GBP 5,000 Research Training and Support Grant.
MaintenanceUKRI-rate maintenance stipend
Duration3.5 years

Eligibility and Requirements

Any nationality or fee status; an interdisciplinary project aligned with a Warwick Research Spotlight or Research Centre. English evidence, approved equivalents and waivers depend on the programme; IELTS is not a universal requirement for every applicant.

Application dates

ComponentDetails
RecruitmentOpen from 5 October 2026
DeadlineCourse: 7 December; scholarship: 10 December; references: 21 December 2026, all 16:59 GMT

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Official Link

Full announcement and application portal: https://scholarships.warwick.ac.uk/apply/scholarship/81b0f648-b744-498d-ae12-b940c10f0c1e

Source: scholarships.warwick.ac.uk - the details in this listing were recorded from this official page.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 10 December 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

Apply for an eligible doctoral course, then submit the shared scholarship application including the Interdisciplinary Chancellors statement.

The application is shared with Warwick’s other streams. This is a distinct named stream, not an additional guaranteed award.

About University of Warwick

The University of Warwick offers doctoral study across its faculties and research centres. Its postgraduate research scholarship competition includes several funding streams with a shared application process.

Official details: Programme information

Application route: Application form or official instructions

2026/27 UKRI reference rate: the minimum UKRI doctoral stipend is £21,805 per year, tax-free (London institutions +£2,000), effective 1 October 2026.
